rule: The Annex II classification includes agents known to cause infectious disease in humans; animal/plant pathogens known not to affect humans and GM microorganisms are outside this list.
operational_rule: Do not infer coverage beyond the statutory list.

rule: Classification is based on effects on healthy workers; additional susceptibility (prior disease, medication, immune disorders, pregnancy or lactation) belongs in the risk assessment.
operational_rule: risk_group is agent-level metadata and must not be treated as worker-specific risk.

rule: Agents not classified in groups 2-4 are not implicitly group 1.
operational_rule: Unknown lookup returns unclassified/NA; never auto-assign group 1.

rule: If an agent is absent from the table, the employer must estimate infection risk using Article 3 definitions and provisionally assimilate it to a group; if in doubt between two groups, use the higher hazard group.
operational_rule: Software may expose a professional-assessment workflow but must not silently classify an unlisted agent.

rule: Viruses isolated in humans but not assessed/classified must be classified at least group 2 unless shown unlikely to cause disease in humans.
operational_rule: Return regulatory_minimum_group=2 and final_reference_level=NA pending professional assessment.

rule: Group 3 agents marked ** may present limited infection risk because they are not normally infectious by the airborne route.
operational_rule: Preserve risk_group=3 and a separate limited_airborne flag; never downgrade group.

rule: Containment requirements derived from parasite classification apply only to life-cycle stages infectious to humans at work.
operational_rule: Expose infectious_stage_context as a future technical field; do not alter legal group.

rule: A=possible allergic effects; D=exposure list retention >10 years; T=toxin production; V=effective vaccine available and registered in EU.
operational_rule: Store flags as independent booleans plus raw notes.

rule: Where work involves exposure to several categories of biological agents, risks are assessed on the basis of the danger posed by all agents present.
operational_rule: Default multi-agent function reports all groups and refuses to collapse discordant groups to one value without an explicit policy.

rule: ERBio determines the reference level by selecting the biological agent(s) most likely in the evaluated area/job, considering most likely pathology or exposed entry routes.
operational_rule: Reference-level selection must preserve the identity of the selected plausible agent(s).
source: Aguilar Elena doctoral thesis (2015), ERBio chapter 4

rule: BASEBiO provides expanded and updated technical information about agents and uses Annex II risk group classification.
operational_rule: BASEBiO enriches agent metadata but never silently overrides the legal registry risk_group.
